title: tier-2 shipped code: a shape entry's world frame against 0x142cb8b80
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-sim/src/collide.rs (shape_world_transform), called by crates/ow-sim/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the collision_transform entry.

The leaf returns the output pointer, so the unit declares its return channel void and the compared channel is the output pointee: the position quad at +0x00 and the quaternion at +0x10. The two pools are reached through the record's +0x2a0 and +0x288 pointers, so the fixture pins both to fixed arena addresses (ARENA_BASE is fixed by emu_oracle) and patches those addresses into the record.

The composed branch multiplies a difference by the zero quad at 0x142f84a00 in two places. Those multiplies are no-ops for finite inputs but propagate a non-finite difference, so the Rust keeps them verbatim rather than folding them away.
No image data is read by the leaf beyond its own constants, and it has no stack cookie.
acknowledgedGaps: This unit verifies the transform only. Which pool a real world fills, and which attach state a real shape entry carries, are set by the body and owner creation calls (0x142cb3940 / 0x142cd4ef0); the unit drives the leaf, not those callers.
The shape-entry array at [record+0x2b8] and the narrowphase's per-type dispatch remain outside this unit; the transform is verified as the leaf the dispatch calls.

Non-finite corpus values are NaN only, and only in the quaternion, because the emulator's softfloat is not faithful to x86 in two ways a richer corpus would expose: an invalid operation (inf * 0, which the (origin - pivot) * 0 term reaches for an infinite origin) answers 0x7fc00000 in the emulator where the x86 hardware QNaN indefinite is 0xffc00000; and when both operands of an ADDPS/SUBPS are NaN the emulator does not always return the destination's NaN. Both were measured on this machine with a runtime (black_box, not constant-folded) SSE probe. The hardware result for the infinite-origin lane is pinned by a Rust unit test in collide.rs instead.
